Cluny monks ruled the town from 999 to 1789. Protestantism won many converts, but Jesuits summoned in 1618, and Visitandines brought by Pere Paul de Barry in 1678, completed the Catholic recovery. Since 1873 Paray has drawn up to 100,000 pilgrims a year. Chief shrines are the Visitation chapel of Margaret Mary Alacoque's visions and the Sacred Heart basilica, a jewel of Cluniac building.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-paul-henri-co:
Paul Henri Corentin Feval was a French novelist born at Rennes on 27 September 1817 and dead at Paris on 8 March 1887. Of an old barrister family, he was schooled at Rennes lycee, read law at Rennes University, and joined the bar at nineteen. Losing his first case disgusted him with law, and in Paris he worked as a bank clerk, then lost that post through reading on duty.

He served an advertising firm, joined an obscure Paris paper's staff, and proofread for Le Nouvelliste, writing all the while. His 1841 short story, The Club of Seals, in La Revue de Paris, won notice and opened leading Paris papers to him. In 1844, as Francis Trolopp, he wrote The Mysteries of London to great success, and thereafter scarcely stopped, sometimes issuing four novels at once. Stage versions mostly failed, save Le Bossu, and his later Catholic turn reshaped his work.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pectoral:
Pectoral, or pectoral of judgment, is a term whose Hebrew meaning is lost, little lit by early translations. The Septuagint gives logion, the Vulgate rationale, whence the Douai version's literal rational, and the Authorized Version gives breastplate. In minute directions for the high priest's official dress in Exodus 28, part of the priestly code, and Exodus 39, special weight falls on the breastplate or pectoral. Josephus's differing account of the same is judged less reliable.

The main reason for care over its making seems its role as receptacle of the sacred oracular lot, the mysterious Urim and Thummim. That role makes probable Ewald's tentative etymology: the pouch of the Oracle. From Exodus, its material matched the ephod's: gold, blue, purple, and scarlet on fine twined linen, among the finest textiles. Its form was a square from folding material a cubit long and half a cubit wide, fitted with gold settings.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pedralvarez-c:
Pedralvarez Cabral, or Pedro Alvarez, was a celebrated Portuguese navigator generally called Brazil's discoverer, born probably around 1460, death date uncertain. Very little is known of his life. Third son of Fernao Cabral, governor of Beira and Belmonte, and Isabel de Gouvea, he married Isabel de Castro, daughter of Fernando de Noronha.

He must have trained well in navigation and sailed widely. King Emmanuel judged him fit to continue Vasco da Gama's work, giving him a fleet bound for India in 1500. His commission was to build lasting trade ties and spread Christianity, using arms when needed. Rich Florentine merchants funded the ships' fitting, and priests joined the voyage. Among captains of thirteen ships with 1,200 men were Bartolomeu Diaz, Pero Vaz de Caminha, and Nicolao Coelho. Da Gama himself set the course. The fleet left Lisbon on 9 March 1500, steering to dodge Guinea's calms, then sailed decidedly southwest.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-port-royal:
Port-Royal was a celebrated Benedictine abbey that deeply shaped France's religious and literary life in the seventeenth century. Mathilde de Garlande founded it in 1204 in the Chevreuse valley, six leagues from Paris. In 1608 Mère Angélique Arnauld reformed it.

In 1626 the unhealthy, cramped house moved to Paris's Faubourg St-Jacques. Under Paris's archbishop, its nuns became Daughters of the Blessed Sacrament. In 1636 Abbé de St-Cyran became spiritual director and made it a Jansenist centre, gathering scholars seeking solitude and study. Lemaître de Lacy was jailed in the Bastille in 1666. The 1669 Peace of the Church revived it briefly. Arnauld fled in 1670. Louis XIV resolved to crush it. After the 1702 case-of-conscience quarrel, a papal bull suppressed Port-Royal des Champs in 1704. The last nuns were expelled in 1709, and its remains were destroyed in 1710.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-portugal:
Portugal sits on the west of the Iberian Peninsula, bounded by Spain on the north and east and by the Atlantic on the west and south. It runs at most 362 miles long and 140 miles wide, with an area of 35,490 square miles. People still name the old provinces: Entre Douro e Minho, Traz os Montes, Beira, Estremadura, Alemtejo, and Algarve. Madeira with Porto Santo and the Azores count as part of continental Portugal.

Papal bulls gave Portugal command of the seas from Africa to India. Sixtus IV confirmed its kings in all lands found from Cape Non to India in 1481. John II pushed discovery with fresh energy, and Bartholomew Diaz rounded the Cape of Good Hope. Alfonso's reign also gave the Alfonsine Code of 1446 and the defeat at Toro in 1476.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-provincial:
A provincial is the officer who, under the superior general of a religious order, watches over all the local superiors in one division of the order. That division is called a province. This encyclopedia entry explains that a province is largely geographical. It covers one or more countries, or part of one country. Yet houses of one province may sit inside another's territory. Authority over members is personal rather than tied to place. The old monastic orders had no such officers at all.

Provincials belong to newer congregations, beginning with the mendicant orders. Their wandering friars needed a middle layer of government between the general and the local house. Their powers vary by order. In congregations with simple vows that are not exempt, the provincial holds no jurisdiction of his own. Under the Regulations of 1901 he also oversaw the finances of the provincial procurator and the local superiors.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-raymond-bonal:
Raymond Bonal, theologian and founder of the Congregation of the Priests of Saint Mary, was born at Villefranche in Rouergue on 15 August 1600 and died at Agde, in Hérault, about 1653. This encyclopedia entry follows him from classics and philosophy with the Jesuits at Cahors to theology and canon and civil law at Toulouse. There he took his doctorate in theology in 1628. In 1632 he conceived a community of priests living out the spirit of Saint Francis de Sales.

With two other churchmen he began community life in a house near the church of Our Lady of Pity at Villefranche, and others soon joined. The parish of Foix came to his community in 1639. A few years later, Villefranche gained a seminary run by Bonal. In 1650 he organized a seminary and college at a further site, and congregation archives supply its sources.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ritual:
The Ritual, or Rituale Romanum, ranks among the Roman Rite's official books. It holds the priest's services that are not in the Missal or Breviary, plus a few from those books. It is the latest and least uniform book of the rite. When ritual functions were first written down, the Western Sacramentary and the Eastern Euchologion held the priest's part. That part ran from the liturgy itself to every sacrament, blessing, and rite.

In the West, books later split by service rather than by user. The Missal, containing the whole Mass, replaced the Sacramentary. Bishops' functions filled the Pontifical, known from the eighth century. Priests' offices lived in a crowd of handbooks. No uniform book for priests existed until 1614. Medieval predecessors bore names such as Manuale, Liber agendarum, and Agenda. Specimens survive from Roeskilde and Schleswig. They show how local the tradition remained.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-roman-process:
The Processional has no recognized place of its own among Roman liturgical books. Strictly it is a single section of the Roman Ritual, its ninth title, with added material from the Missal and Pontifical. The authentic edition's title page runs in Latin as Processionale Romanum, giving the order of sacred processions drawn from the Ritual with similar matter from Missal and Pontifical.

The Ritual does not always print hymns, litanies, and prayers in full, so a Processional sets them out at length with their music. Processionals for local uses were common in later medieval manuscripts, such as the Sarum use. By the close of the fifteenth century and the start of the sixteenth, many printed processionals belonged to churches in France, England, and Germany.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-sao-carlos-do:
São Carlos do Pinhal, a Brazilian diocese suffragan of São Paulo, was created on 7 June 1908. Its bishop, José Marcondes Homem de Mello, born on 13 February 1860 and raised to the episcopate in May 1906, had served as archbishop of Pará before resigning. His short entry in the 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia sketches a new see in a coffee state.

The bishop lives at São Carlos do Pinhal in São Paulo state, founded in 1857 and raised to city rank on 21 April 1880. A railway links it with the state capital, São Paulo, in about six hours. Its 67,000 people are mostly Catholics. Besides public and diocesan schools, the town boasts the Colégio de São Carlos, a girls' school run by the Sisters of the Most Holy Sacrament.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-scandal:
Scandal, in moral theology, is treated in this long entry in the 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia from Thomas Aquinas's definition: a word or deed evil in itself that brings about another's spiritual ruin. It must be an outward act, since an inward act cannot sway another's conduct. It may also be the omission of an outward act, since failing to do what one should equals doing what is forbidden. The entry parses the idea with scholastic care.

Scandal is not the physical cause of a neighbour's sin, but its moral cause or occasion. In a strict sense it means ordering, asking, or advising another to sin, called direct scandal. In a wider sense it means influencing another's sin without direct concern, as by sinning in his presence. The entry then weighs degrees of guilt, the duty of avoiding scandal, and cases where good acts must still be done despite weak consciences.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-seal:
Seals, long used by wealthy and powerful men before the Christian era, were naturally taken up by church leaders once they gained social and political weight. An incidental note in one of Augustine's letters shows that he used a seal. Its entry in the 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia traces ecclesiastical seals from casual use to canon law.

By the Merovingian age the practice seems assumed, since Clovis's laws take it for granted. Later synods ordered bishops' sealed letters for priests lawfully leaving their dioceses, as at Chalon-sur-Saône in 813. Pope Nicholas I complained in the same century that Dol and Reims had sent him letters unsealed, against custom. From that date bishops' seals may be taken as general, at first merely guarding documents from prying eyes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-conal:
St. Conal, or Conall, was an Irish bishop active in the second half of the fifth century, ruling the church of Drum, County Roscommon. The place was subsequently named Drumconnell after him. This entry follows a man whose church Colgan and his copyists inaccurately locate at Kilconnell in County Galway. It is now certain his church was south of Boyle, and Blessed Conal of Drum is his name.

The mistake of crediting Kilconnell and Aughrim, County Galway, as Conal's foundations can also be cleared up by the life of St. Attracta. It records that she came to the neighbourhood of Boyle to build a cell near the church of her uterine brother, St. Conal. St. Dachonna of Eas Dachonna, now Assylin, talked her out of her project at the saint's bidding.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-elizabeth-:
Elizabeth of Portugal earned the name Peacemaker by riding between armies, twice, to stop wars within her own family. Born in 1271 to Pedro III of Aragon, she was named for her great-aunt Elizabeth of Hungary and called Isabel in Portuguese history. Married young to Diniz, a hard-working but unfaithful king, she kept her strict round of prayer, fasting, and care for the poor. The Catholic Encyclopedia piece of 1913 dates her death to 1336.

In 1323 her son Affonso rebelled against his father over favours shown to royal bastards. Elizabeth rode in person between the opposing armies and reconciled them. Widowed in 1325, she retired to a Poor Clare convent she had founded at Coimbra. In 1336 she repeated the feat at Estremoz, halting a war with Castile before dying of fever. Urban VIII canonized her in 1625.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-gal:
Two bishops named Gal held Clermont, and this entry honours both, with the first the more illustrious. Of ninety-eight bishops of Clermont-Ferrand, twenty-nine are saints, including Gal the first, bishop from 527 to 551, and Gal the second, from 640 to 650. Born to a senatorial Auvergne family, the first Gal embraced monastic life, then counselled Quintianus, whom he would succeed. The Catholic Encyclopedia piece of 1913 follows him through invasion and captivity.

Thierry I of Austrasia seized Auvergne, took Gal prisoner, and attached him to his palace oratory. Freed years later, Gal returned to Clermont and succeeded Quintianus in 527. As bishop he defended church rights intrepidly against Thierry's governor Sivigald, then sheltered Sivigald's children from the prince's wrath. His chief event was Clermont's council of 535, with fifteen prelates attending.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-jane-franc:
Jane Frances de Chantal, widow at twenty-eight, turned a ruined feudal household into order, then founded the Visitation. Born at Dijon on 28 January 1572 to the president of Burgundy's parliament, royalist leader in the League wars, she married Baron de Chantal in 1592 and lived at Bourbilly castle. She restored a household on ruin's brink to prosperity. The Catholic Encyclopedia piece of 1913 dates her death at Moulins' Visitation convent to 13 December 1641.

During her husband's absences at court or army, she dressed soberly, answering critics that the eyes she must please were a hundred miles away. God, the entry says, blessed with miracles her care for Christ's suffering members. Francis de Sales praised her as Solomon's perfect woman, hard to find in Jerusalem. In 1601 a harquebus accident killed her husband while shooting, leaving her widowed with four children. From that loss grew her religious life.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-martial:
Martial, bishop of Limoges in the third century, is known only through Gregory of Tours, and legend soon made him an apostle. No accurate information survives on his origin, birth, or acts. All knowledge comes from Gregory: under Decius and Gratus's consulate, seven bishops went out from Rome to Gaul. The Catholic Encyclopedia piece of 1913 names them. Gatien went to Tours, Trophimus to Arles, Paul to Narbonne, Saturninus to Toulouse, Denis to Paris, Austromoine to Clermont, and Martial to Limoges.

Martial seems to have come with two priests from the Orient, so he may have been born there. He converted Limoges's inhabitants, and his memory stayed venerated there. Very early, popular imagination transformed him into a first-century apostle. Sent by Peter himself, he evangelized Limoges province and all Aquitaine, raising a dead man by touching him with Peter's rod.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-william-of:
William of Maleval, also called William the Great, lived as a hermit in the Sienese desert after pilgrimage to Jerusalem. His disciple Albert's life, written from his last year at Maleval, is lost. The Bollandist life by Theodobald is unreliable, interpolated with lives of at least two other Williams, and confuses him at length with William of Gellone.

What stands is this: he met Eugene III at Rome, who ordered a penitential pilgrimage to Jerusalem. He stayed there one or two years, not nine as Theodobald claims. About 1153 he returned to Italy. He lived as a hermit near Pisa, then on Monte Pruno. From 1155 he lived in the desert valley of Stabulum Rodis, later Maleval, where disciples joined him. He died on 10 February 1157 and was beatified in 1202.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-the-escorial:
Spain's eighth wonder, the Escorial, is the vast building described here on the Sierra Guadarrama's southeastern slope, some twenty-seven miles northwest of Madrid. Proper title El Real Monasterio de San Lorenzo del Escorial takes Escorial from a nearby town. Monastery, church, royal pantheon, palace for summer and autumn court, college, library, and art galleries combine in one rectangle.

Philip II ordered it begun in 1563 under Juan Bautista de Toledo, aided by Escalante and Tolosa. It marked Spain's victory over France at Saint-Quentin in 1557 and met Charles V's will for a royal mausoleum. Bautista's ambitious, severe Doric plan passed at his 1567 death to Herrera and Minjores. Grid plan, courts, and collections fill a monument to king, faith, and art.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-transvaal:
The Transvaal was a vicariate apostolic in southern Africa, lying between 23 degrees 3 minutes and 27 degrees 30 minutes south, and 25 and 32 degrees east. Its people numbered about 960,000, with some 320,000 whites and 640,000 Black Africans. Its rolling plains could raise almost unlimited grain, and stock raising thrived there, while the discovery of gold drew a flood of British settlers to work its mines.

From the Great Trek of 1835 to 1838, Boer farmers left Cape Colony, fought natives and British in turn, and won independence by the Sand River Convention of January 1852. Britain annexed the country in April 1877 after Boer defeat by African peoples in 1876, but war in 1881 restored Boer independence. The vicariate's schools, homes and hospitals, run by sisters of seven congregations totalling 147 sisters, served its scattered Catholic flock.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ulrich-of-ric:
Ulrich of Richenthal was the chronicler of the Council of Constance, born at an unknown date and dead about 1438. He was a citizen of Constance, well educated and a good Latinist, a landowner and a layman. He may have been the son of Johannes Richenthal, town clerk of Constance in the later fourteenth century. During the council he dealt often with the fathers gathered there, meeting papal agents who found lodgings for members and doing business for princes present in the city.

Ulrich watched the council closely, noting its great events, feasts, and celebrations, with his native town as their stage. He wrote in the German dialect of Constance, and his chronicle survives as a vivid town's-eye view of a world council. The entry describes the man, his vantage point, and the worth of his homely record beside the formal acts of the council.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-vicar-general:
The vicar-general is a diocese's highest official after the bishop himself, a cleric deputed to exercise the bishop's jurisdiction generally, so that his acts count as the bishop's own. His wide administrative powers once belonged to the archdeacon, first among the seven deacons. Appointed freely by the bishop to run external administration, control the lower clergy, and visit and correct clerics by judicial process.

By the eleventh century archdeacons held ordinary, stable jurisdiction with courts of first instance, and grew so powerful that they hampered bishops themselves. From the twelfth century onward bishops therefore turned to new assistants, later called vicars-general or officials, removable at the ordinary's will. The entry follows that shift from entrenched archdeacons to deputies who serve at the bishop's pleasure.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-westminster-c:
Westminster Cathedral in London stands, as a national sign of Roman Catholic faith in England since the Reformation, pre-eminent, first among them thanks to vast proportions and original design. The project for a metropolitan cathedral began in 1865 under the restored hierarchy's first archbishop, but building started only thirty years later under Cardinal Vaughan, from John Francis Bentley's design. On Bentley's death in 1902 the structure was nearly complete, though inside decoration had barely begun.

Covering about 54,000 square feet, its main feature apart from the campanile is a spacious, open nave sixty feet wide under domical vaulting. Its support system is like Gothic cathedrals' huge yet narrow buttresses at intervals, stiffened by transverse walls, arcading, and vaulting. Entering, the visitor misses the spacious outer narthex of St Mark's or Constantinople's churches, but soon forgets it amid fine proportions and Byzantine-capitalled marble columns supporting galleries.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-youghal:
Youghal is the Irish wardenship in Cloyne diocese founded by Thomas, eighth Earl of Desmond, under charter of 27 December 1464 and confirmed by Rome. It held many Cloyne rectories and vicarages plus four in Ardfert, paying about six hundred pounds a year to a warden, eight fellows, and eight singing-men. Three years later the founder was hanged by Ireland's viceroy on 15 February 1468.

The ninth earl was murdered by servants on 7 December 1487. Cloyne's bishop resigned two years later, and his successor, Blessed Thady MacCarthy, beatified in 1895, died in exile at Ivrea in 1492. The last Catholic warden was Thomas Allen in 1533, followed by the schismatic Roger Skiddy, later Dean of Limerick and Elizabeth's Bishop of Cork. Sixty years later the Earl of Cork seized the endowments, and a merely titular Catholic line lasted to Father Richard Harnet in 1709. The warden's house is now Sir Walter Raleigh's House.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-zeal:
Zeal is love in vehement action, defined from a root meaning to boil or throb with heat. Saint Thomas calls it the vehement movement of one who loves toward the object of love, its intensity proportioned to the love felt. Love divides into self-regarding love and altruistic love, but usage restricts zeal to the altruistic kind; in religion it means ardent endeavours to promote God's glory.

Because it presupposes judgment about means, true zeal differs from false zeal by the soundness of that judgment. Saint Paul's zeal was false when he persecuted the Church and true when he became its apostle. His words, the love of Christ urges us, describe the prompting that laid the Church's foundations and sent apostles, missionaries, priests, and religious into lives of self-sacrifice and works of charity.
chaitanya-and-the-vaishnava-poets-of-ben:
John Beames's Chaitanya and the Vaishnava Poets of Bengal studies fifteenth- and sixteenth-century Bengali verse, as printed in the Indian Antiquary for 1873. Beames takes as his centre the Padakalpataru, the wish-granting tree of song, a collection he calls the scriptures of the Vaishnava sect in Bengal.

The collection gathers songs by various poets of various ages, arranged to show the full series of topics and tenets of the sect. It moves through consecration and invocations to Radha and Krishna's growing love, closing with valedictory hymns. Beames writes as a civil servant scholar of the Indian Civil Service, explaining a devotional literature little known to English readers. Students of Indian religion and poetry will find it a pioneering survey.
daphne-an-autumn-pastoral:
Margaret Pollock Sherwood set her short novel Daphne at the Villa Accolanti in Italy, where an American girl spends an autumn among old servants and older hills. Daphne wrestles with a phrase-book while the butler Giacomo and his wife Assunta understand her perfectly and answer in torrents. Sherwood makes the language gap the book's gentle comedy.

Walks above the villa, a stream, ilex shade, and dinners ordered by dictionary fill the days. The pastoral of the subtitle is the point: slowness, beauty, and a young woman thinking her own thoughts far from home. Sherwood wrote a quiet romance of place, in which Italy itself, courteous, sunlit, and amused, does most of the wooing of the reader.
discourse-of-the-life-and-character-of-t:
A funeral oration on a Virginia statesman fills Hugh Blair Grigsby's discourse, printed at Norfolk in 1860 by J. D. Ghiselin. Grigsby spoke it on June 29, 1860, in the Freemason Street Baptist Church, before the bar of Norfolk and the citizens at large. The subject is the Honourable Littleton Waller Tazewell.

Grigsby first recalls the bar's own mourning: the members bore their friend's body to a steamer and crossed by candlelight the bay he had loved. Tazewell's voice, once equal to every occasion, had first failed him in a speech, as he told Grigsby on leaving the hall. A second speech, following Mr Monroe, found him in a better place and full-toned again. The discourse is long, warm, and full of the old Virginia bar.
doe-osti-17032782-nubow-3d-user-and-theo:
User and theory manual ANL/NSE-26/65, by Nicholas Wozniak of Argonne National Laboratory, documents NUBOW-3D, a Fortran code for fast reactor core analysis. Over a reactor life, heat and radiation make fuel assembly ducts bow and press on each other. The code predicts that bowing and the contact forces across a full core.

Ducts are treated as beams that bend in two directions, with traits varying along their length. The manual explains thermal bowing, gap and contact handling, the iterative solver that settles forces, and strain from creep and swelling under radiation. Main uses are judging core restraint systems and feeding displacement maps into reactivity calculations.
doe-osti-17069412-project-title-efficien:
Final technical report from Fanglin Chen at the University of South Carolina, with Kevin Huang as co-lead, closes a project running June 2021 to May 2026 under award DE-EE0009427. The aim was a cleaner refinery route to ethylene, a basic chemical building block made at over 140 million tons a year. Partners included Idaho and Lawrence Berkeley labs.

Work centered on solid oxide cells, ceramic devices that can split carbon dioxide and convert methane in one system. The team made porous metal supports, new cathode materials for carbon dioxide electrolysis, and a catalyst for coupling methane into ethylene. Combined cell tests ran both reactions at once, and a cost and engineering study weighed the full process.
doe-osti-17084219-ocuphlux-user-manual:
User manual SAND2026-26944, printed September 2026, documents OcuPhlux, a Sandia software tool written by Aaron Spieles and Kaden Plewe of the Concentrating Solar Technologies group. The tool works from paired photographs of the sun and a subject, plus camera settings, to compute light values with stated uncertainty. Eye inputs, such as pupil radius and focal length, appear among its settings.

Manual chapters walk through the graphical interface block by block, sidebar controls, and recommended hardware for collecting data. Input tables give each field type, unit, and allowed range, from pixel thresholds to filter factors. An uncertainty tab takes a spread value for every camera and sun input, so users can carry measurement doubt into the result.
doe-osti-17171709-disk-cut-processing-mi:
Jonathan Gigax, Douglas Smith, Thomas Ontiveros, and Los Alamos colleagues compare ways of cutting disks from joined metal plates, in a report issued 6 August 2026. Two assemblies were studied: aluminum on titanium, and tantalum on titanium. Cutting can distort the bond line and damage the microstructure near the cut, which matters for later use of the disks.

Disks were sectioned by hole saw and by femtosecond laser at several kerf widths. Samples were quartered and read under electron microscopy. Hole saw cuts consistently did more damage than laser cuts at either setting. Aluminum on titanium samples showed strong distortion of the titanium at the interface under the saw, and separation with oxidation under the laser. Tantalum on titanium changed far less under both. Laser surfaces were rougher in most materials except tantalum.
doe-osti-17197398-joining-core-program-j:
Wei Zhang, Jian Chen, Zhili Feng, and colleagues from three national laboratories report fiscal 2026 work in Thrust 3 of the Joining Core Program 3.0, in report ORNL/SPR-2026/4821 dated August 2026. The consortium, spanning Oak Ridge, Argonne, and Pacific Northwest, develops joining methods for multi material vehicle building at high volume. Thrust 3 covers the measurement and computing side of that effort.

Its charge is advanced characterization of joints and welds, plus computational methods that predict joint behavior. Artificial intelligence and machine learning drive process monitoring and control across the program. The annual report records the year's tasks, findings, and publications for this thrust. Partner rosters and division credits fill the front matter.
doe-osti-2570972-high-energy-density-phy:
A final technical report by Ivan Oleynik of the University of South Florida, covering September 2022 through September 2023 under award DE-SC0023508, studies ablator materials for inertial confinement fusion. The December 2022 ignition shot at the National Ignition Facility used a diamond ablator, the shell that compresses the fuel. Flaws at the diamond and fuel boundary hurt performance, so the project examined amorphous carbon as a replacement.

Amorphous carbon nearly matches the strength of diamond. It also takes high-atomic-number dopants that diamond resists, and its makeup can be tuned as it is made. The team paired shock tests at the Omega EP laser in Rochester with machine-learning molecular dynamics runs on large DOE machines. Goals included mapping where the material stays metastable, probing shifts toward diamond or supercooled liquid, and building an equation of state checked against the tests. The results feed the design of future fusion targets.
doe-osti-2574313-deformation-mechanisms-:
Progress report DE-SC0016337, from Purdue University under Xinghang Zhang with Jian Wang of the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, covers September 2021 to August 2024. The subject is nanotwinned aluminum. Twin boundaries make copper and silver both strong and ductile, but aluminum's high stacking fault energy was supposed to keep twins out. The group's microscopes found twins and a 9R phase in aluminum anyway, with high flow stresses to match.

The report tests three linked hypotheses. First, judging whether solutes help twins form takes the full energetics of defects, not stacking fault energy alone. Iron, cobalt, and nickel all promote growth twins, even though calculations show they raise that energy. Second, the twin structures may give aluminum unusual deformation behavior; nanotwinned aluminum-iron already shows high compressive strength and work hardening. Third, alloy strength itself may rest on these same defect interactions. Experiments and density functional calculations run side by side.
doe-osti-2583475-epitaxial-growth-develo:
Under CRADA CRD-18-00755, NREL helped Trumpf Photonics coat laser diode facets, work closed out in report NREL/TP-5K00-94079 dated March 13, 2025. Kirstin Alberi was the laboratory's technical contact; Valentin Loyo-Maldonado was the company's. The problem sits on the edge of a laser diode. The cleaved facets of AlGaAs/InGaAs lasers degrade, and a zinc selenide coating grown on those facets can passivate them, protecting performance and reliability.

Four tasks divided the work. Trumpf's own material growth was characterized first. NREL then developed a thorough cleaning procedure for the facets, since epitaxy fails on dirty surfaces. Next came the zinc selenide growth recipe itself, tuned on the (110) facet orientation these lasers expose. The final task transferred both procedures to Trumpf's site for production use. The agreement ran three years, pairing a national laboratory's surface science with a manufacturer's diode line.
doe-osti-2584539-light-high-performance-:
Final technical report DE-FE0031980, from C-Crete Technologies under Rouzbeh Savary, turns coal into a building material that is mostly coal. The goal was a composite up to about ninety-five percent coal by weight. It had to beat ordinary Portland cement products on physical, chemical, and thermal performance, with minimal external binder. Cement making is a giant slice of industrial emissions; a structural material built from domestic coal would flip a liability into feedstock.

The project cleared much of that bar. Samples above eighty percent coal matched cement-based concrete's properties. Select samples topped 7,000 psi compressive strength and 420 psi flexural strength. The composites resisted acidic and basic attack in durability tests. Slab and beam scale pieces were cast with the company's process, though the team notes it was not semi-continuous. The verdict: coal composites are credible precast candidates, with production flow the next problem to solve.
doe-osti-2584747-nif-enhanced-yield-capa:
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory report LLNL-TR-2008875 records the conceptual design review of the National Ignition Facility Enhanced Yield Capability project. A large design team, including Pamela Divoky, Jeff Horner, and Brian Kruschwitz, prepared the material under review. Dan Mason and Douglas Larson co-chaired the review, which met on June 26 and 27, 2025. Parts of the hosted text carry garbled character encoding, though the summary and charge remain legible.

The review's purpose was to judge key aspects of the design and assess readiness to move to the next project phase. The committee checked the design against a checklist negotiated with the National Nuclear Security Administration's review process. Its charge questions covered whether the conceptual design can meet its requirements and support refined cost and schedule estimates. Findings, recommendations, and observations were recorded for the design team.
doe-osti-2586511-cloud-atmosphere-impact:
Matthew Shupe of the University of Colorado wrote this final report for Department of Energy award DE-SC0021341, covering September 2021 through August 2025. Amy Solomon and Anne Sledd share credit for the project. The team studied how clouds and air-sea ice interaction shape the surface energy budget of the central Arctic, using observations from the MOSAiC expedition and coordinated model experiments.

Three findings anchor the report. A new method applied to thermistor string data shows snow thermal conductivity is systematically higher than most models assume, which strongly affects heat flow and sea ice growth under clear skies. A full annual cycle of observations shows how cloud types steer the seasonal energy balance, with melt taking the excess energy in summer. Finally, the observations were used to test forecast models, and most showed persistent flaws in representing liquid-bearing Arctic clouds.
doe-osti-2587356-design-basis-document-o:
Bruce Kelly of SolarDynamics prepared this design basis document under Department of Energy grant DE-EE0009810, issued as Revision 0 on July 11, 2025. It is an owner's technical specification for nitrate salt systems in concentrating solar power projects. Molten nitrate salt is the heat transfer and storage fluid in such plants. It punishes piping, tanks, and valves that are not built for it.

The document runs to three volumes. Volume 1 gives specifications for parabolic trough projects. Volume 2 covers central receiver projects, and Volume 3 gives the narrative behind the numbers. The first volume alone exceeds 200 pages of requirements. Operational detail runs deep. If a receiver trips on loss of flow, it is typically drained. Restarting the heliostat field and receiver then costs an outage of at least 90 minutes, and as much as three hours. Owners and builders use such a specification to bid and build salt systems that match.
doe-osti-2587514-user-guide-a-curated-da:
Elizabeth Silber leads a five-author team in this user guide, SAND2025-10874, printed in August 2025. Peter Brown, Emerson Brown, Andrea Thompson, and Vedant Sawal join her. The guide documents a curated dataset of regional meteor events, each recorded two ways at once: by optical cameras and by infrasound sensors listening for the low-frequency sound of the fireball.

Paired records of this kind are rare and valuable, since light gives the trajectory while sound probes the energy deposited in the air. The guide walks the directory structure folder by folder. Optical data covers raw imagery, astrometry files, and their solutions. Atmospheric profiles come in high-resolution G2S format for each event, plus legacy profiles in text and spreadsheet form, and the infrasound data ships in miniSEED format. A user can go from download to analysis without guessing what any file holds.
doe-osti-2587768-empirical-indicators-of:
Joachim Seel, Dev Millstein, and Julie Mulvaney Kemp of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory wrote this August 2025 study, supported by the Department of Energy's Grid Deployment Office. It measures the value of transmission in the Southeast United States with empirical indicators: the price differences between neighboring grid regions, which show what one more wire between them would be worth.

Inside Florida, annual average trade values among Duke Energy Florida, Tampa Electric, the Florida Municipal Power Pool, and Florida Power and Light range from 4 to 19 dollars per megawatt-hour. Across three larger corridors the values run from 5 to 28 dollars, with the link between PJM and Duke Energy Carolinas consistently highest. The long-term average between Southern Company and Duke Energy Florida is 9.7 dollars. Timing matters enormously: in 2018, half of that corridor's annual value accrued in just 3 percent of all hours, mostly during cold snaps such as polar vortex events.
doe-osti-2588600-design-basis-document-o:
Bruce Kelly of Solar Dynamics LLC led this final technical report for award DE-EE0009810, covering May 2022 through October 2025. It produces a design basis document and owner's technical specification for nitrate salt systems in concentrating solar power projects. These systems store solar heat after sunset in molten salt tanks, piping, and heat exchangers.

Salt technology's problem is inexperience. Perhaps 60 commercial parabolic trough plants use nitrate salt storage. About 20 central receiver plants use it as the working fluid. Fossil and nuclear plants number in the thousands, their designs debugged over generations. Salt projects bidding into a mature market have sometimes promised more than they delivered. The study mines operating projects for what worked, catalogs system failures, and drafts design changes to fix known problems. Three volumes totaling some 590 pages split trough, central receiver, and design change guidance. One hard question: when should fatigue life checks on storage vessels be mandatory?
doe-osti-2589395-solar-radiation-measure:
A long-running cooperative project on solar radiation measurement closes with National Renewable Energy Laboratory final report NREL/TP-5D00-95609. Technical contact Aron Habte, with Patrick Bunn and Leland Boeman listed in the record, covers agreement CRD-11-00434. Measurements were collected at a modern station run by the University of Arizona, using government-furnished equipment the laboratory maintained.

Long records of sunlight and weather are needed to design solar systems and to check satellite-based solar data sets. The station's data were delivered by the laboratory and posted publicly through its Measurement and Instrumentation Data Center. Data loss stayed small across the years covered: every year lost less than 2 percent, and most years less than 1 percent. Losses came mainly from instrument faults, logger gaps, and tracker failures. The report closes the agreement with a full accounting.
doe-osti-2589396-development-of-integrat:
National Renewable Energy Laboratory final report NREL/TP-5700-95613 closes cooperative project CRD-23-24565 with Solar Dynamics. Technical contact Devon Kesseli led laboratory work on the Distant Observer software, a camera-based tool that checks the shape of newly built parabolic troughs. Troughs are curved mirrors that focus sunlight to heat fluid in solar power plants.

Field assembly crews need fast checks they can run with little training. Work focused on making software readings consistent, proving that trough adjustments show up in its measurements, and improving speed, ease of use, and the camera math behind it. Output was tuned to give specific adjustment directions for the company's SunBeam trough. The filing records a tool moving from laboratory code toward daily quality control on construction sites.
doe-osti-2589493-oxidative-funneling-of-:
National Renewable Energy Laboratory final report NREL/TP-2800-95354 closes cooperative project CRD-22-22804 on recycling a stubborn plastic. Technical contact Katrina Knauer covers PVDC, a barrier plastic made by Syensqo that is rarely recycled, often in multi-layer packaging. The team tested a two-step route called oxidative funneling.

Step one uses a metal-driven oxidation to break mixed plastics into smaller oxygen-rich compounds. Step two feeds those compounds to an engineered bacterium, Pseudomonas putida, which gathers them into a single useful product, a biodegradable polymer used in packaging and medical goods. Runs on PVDC alone produced diacids and chlorinated small molecules. Chloroacetone and chlorinated aromatics also appeared, a safety concern the report flags plainly. The record shows both the promise and the hazard in the route.
doe-osti-2997049-development-and-evaluat:
Florida International University's final report on grant DE-FE0031904, led by Dwayne McDaniel with Pratik Mahyawansi, covers work from August 2020 to May 2025 on predicting drag in gas-solid flows. Drag decides how gas pushes particles in fluidized beds and reactors. Old formulas fit round particles well and odd shapes poorly.

The team gathered more than 4,000 measured and simulated data points covering round and irregular particles, keyed to shape traits such as sphericity, aspect ratio, and orientation. A hybrid model, pairing a classic correlation with a deep neural network, beat both plain formulas and plain machine learning. Extra simulations of packed and fluidized beds taught it how crowding changes drag. The model was wired into the MFiX solver and checked against experiments, doing best in fluidized conditions and weakest in settled beds.
doe-osti-2998224-exact-signed-distance-f:
Eduardo Lozano and Tariq Aslam speed a geometric tool that multiphysics codes use constantly, in Los Alamos report LA-UR-25-30008, issued 8 October 2025. A signed distance field gives, for every point in a grid, the distance to the nearest material surface, with sign marking inside or outside. Codes use it to track moving interfaces between materials.

The method builds the exact field from triangular meshes and straight paths on regular grids, using the fast sweeping method in parallel. It walks outward from the closest surface piece rather than approximating from neighbors, and other shapes can be added whenever a distance formula exists for them. Bounding boxes around each triangle keep the search cheap. Simulation teams gain exact interface distances without the usual accuracy-versus-speed trade.
doe-osti-3000071-exxon-mobil-netl-testin: David Luebke and Jim Bielenberg's short abstract covers modification 54 to a research agreement, AGMT-0922, between the National Energy Technology Laboratory and ExxonMobil. The work tests direct air capture materials at the laboratory's DAC testbed. These materials pull carbon dioxide straight from the air. Three tasks are set. First, check multi-cycle test data on powdered and shaped materials. Second, test steam regeneration of powders at small scale. Third, run larger shaped materials at pilot scale under real process cycles, to define best practice. The sheet is a brief abstract only.
doe-osti-3000606-quantifying-uncertainty:
Leiph Preston and Andrea Darrh of Sandia National Laboratories tackle honest error bars for earthquake source readings, in report SAND2025-13324, printed October 2025. A moment tensor sums up how rock actually moved in a quake or explosion, read from wiggles recorded at scattered stations. Monitors use such readings to tell earthquakes from blasts, so knowing how wrong they might be is as vital as the reading itself.

Three characterisation methods were tested against the things that corrupt them: errors in the Earth model used for the maths, noise in the traces, and poor station geometry. Trials used a detailed three-dimensional model of the western United States as ground truth, then inverted with simpler layered models. Earth model errors biased results in ways a standard 95 percent confidence test could not spot. Noise and model error must therefore be studied together, the authors conclude, or uncertainty will be understated.
doe-osti-3001106-evaluating-variable-imp:
David Sirajuddin, Roman Shapovalov, Brian Hutsel and Sandia colleagues challenge a design dogma in SAND2025-13554R, printed 26 October 2025. Pulsed power machines deliver huge electrical pulses for fusion and weapons work. They carry power through magnetically insulated transmission lines, called MITLs. For decades the rule was that these lines need constant geometric impedance for efficient flow. This project asked whether varying the impedance on purpose could instead cut risk in next generation drivers.

Theory came first. The team built equilibrium models for variable impedance lines, work sent to a journal. Circuit codes and high fidelity particle in cell simulations then tested the concept across many line levels and segment designs. Findings weigh the possible gains in reliability against efficiency costs. The report is dense simulation work, tables of segment shapes included. Its conclusion reframes variable impedance as a deliberate risk lever, not a defect to be engineered away.
doe-osti-3001333-software-quality-assura:
Kalin Kiesling of Argonne sets the quality rules for a simulation code in this Software Quality Assurance Plan for Cardinal, a 32 page governance document. Cardinal wraps two codes inside the MOOSE framework. They are NekRS, a spectral element fluid dynamics solver, and OpenMC, a Monte Carlo transport code. They give reactor analysts coupled thermal hydraulics and neutronics on graphics processors. Software this big needs process discipline to match.

The plan spells out how changes are proposed, reviewed, tested and approved, and what records each step leaves. Tables summarise the tests and reviews in change control, and the training each project role requires. Configuration management, problem reporting and corrective action get procedures. As a plan rather than results, it reads as the constitution for Cardinal's development under the NEAMS programme. It states who may change what, how errors are caught, and how trust is maintained release after release.
doe-osti-3001551-summary-of-pilot-projec:
Bhaskar Mitra, Li He and Vanessa Hamilton of PNNL summarise an assistance project for Oregon in August 2025. Oregon's Energy Security Plan had flagged the fuel supply chain as a weak point. The state imports nearly all its transport fuel through few routes: the Olympic pipeline, trucks and barges. Sponsored by the Energy Department's CESER office, the team planned a quantitative risk analysis of electric and petroleum fuels, reusing a 2024 sector coupling framework.

Data defeated the plan. Daily fuel flow figures by mode and region largely do not exist in public hands. A table of needs against receipts makes the gap plain, and that absence is itself a headline finding. The study pivoted to scenarios and a risk matrix. It simulated events that could pinch fuel availability in some regions. Recommendations address the data limits and Oregon's energy burden, and the framework is offered to other states.
doe-osti-3003054-solving-the-pulsed-powe:
James Hammer, with Trevor Hutchinson, Anthony Johnson, Kumar Raman, and Paul S., gives an abbreviated final report for Lawrence Livermore LDRD project 25-FS-033, dated November 2025. The problem is standoff for pulsed-power fusion energy. A fusion shot releases hundreds to a thousand megajoules in a chamber. The electrical driver must connect to the target through hardware that the blast will not make ruinously expensive to replace.

The proposed answer is very low mass transmission lines, thin wires or foils that carry the pulse and are consumed. The team analyzed how to feed the lines in, hold the power-flow gap, and pump the chamber back down after each shot. Losses from resistance and magnetic forces were evaluated for candidate pulses. Concepts using ten kilograms or less of electrode mass per shot looked workable. One record of invention was filed.
doe-osti-3005426-high-gradient-magnetic-:
Alexander I. Wiechert, Joanna McFarlane, Costas Tsouris, and colleagues give a final 2025 report, ORNL/TM-2025/4194, on high gradient magnetic separation. The technique pulls weakly magnetic particles from a flowing stream by magnetizing a filter matrix inside a strong field. At Oak Ridge it is aimed at nuclear separations, including actinide particles that ordinary chemistry handles slowly.

The year's work optimized the magnetic filter for holding particles once caught. Recovering them selectively, by sonication, still needs tuning, the authors say. Hardware and procedures are judged at technology readiness level 4 overall, with the whole project scored 5: basic components integrated and tested in a laboratory setting. The report is candid about that maturity, which is what a final report owes its sponsor before scale-up money is discussed.
doe-osti-3006481-siting-analyses-for-ele:
Oak Ridge final CRADA report ORNL/TM-2025/4316, by O. A. Omitaomu and B. A. Miller and dated November 2025, covers siting analyses run for Elementl Power under agreement NFE-23-09638. The work used OR-SAGE, Oak Ridge's siting analysis tool for power generation, which weighs site traits such as which plant type suits a site and how far it sits from existing infrastructure. The same tool can screen several generation sources at once, which feeds policy and economic decisions.

The project delivered data packages for more than 30 sites to Elementl Power. The authors credit the packages with shortening the siting evaluation timeline, supplying evidence-based geographic findings, and strengthening the credibility of siting proposals put before the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Sections also address benefits to the funding office's mission, subject inventions, commercialization options, and future collaboration plans.
doe-osti-3008341-high-temperature-seals-:
Final report for DOE contract DE-FE0031924, led by Rahul Bidkar of GE Aerospace Research with seven named co-authors, covers high-temperature seals for supercritical carbon dioxide turbines. The project ran from October 2020 to December 2024 and was submitted in December 2025.

An instrumented commercial dry gas seal ran inside the GE-SwRI Apollo compressor at 27,000 revolutions per minute and saw temperatures upward of 350 degrees Fahrenheit, near the seal's upper limit. A steady-state heat transfer model, the first of its kind for a seal in a running compressor, matched measured seal temperatures within roughly 1 to 16 percent depending on location. A second task designed and tested large-diameter seals for the same duty.
doe-osti-3011045-de-sc0022708-research-p:
A trailerable plug in solar canopy called MEGA is carried through an SBIR Phase II project in the final report for award DE-SC0022708 by GismoPower of Sarasota, Florida. The Mobile Electricity Generating Appliance delivers appliance class generation for homes, small businesses, and renters who cannot modify premises wiring. The project ran from August 2023 to August 2025 under principal investigator Achim Ginsberg Klemmt.

Much of the report concerns standards barriers. GismoPower pressed UL over language in UL 9741 read as requiring permanent connection, arguing it conflicted with National Electrical Code provisions that allow cord and plug connection under set conditions. A formal proposal to revise UL 9741 went through the consensus process.
doe-osti-3011557-improved-fundamental-un:
Aluminium chemistry in simulated tank waste is tracked with in situ mass spectrometry in an Oak Ridge National Laboratory progress report, ORNL/SPR-2025/4190, by Xiao-Ying Yu, Jiyoung Son, Tobias Misicko, and Kaleigh Louque. The project examines aluminate anion behaviour alongside co anions in caustic solutions like those in Hanford style tanks. Two in situ methods carry the measurements.

Vacuum ultraviolet single photon ionisation mass spectrometry samples the liquid chemistry directly. Liquid time of flight secondary ion mass spectrometry uses the SALVI microfluidic device, detecting species such as AlO2 and Al3O5 ions. The September 2025 report records method setup, optimisation on deionised water, and early composition results.
doe-osti-3011814-standard-operating-proc:
Meteorological instruments at the Solar Radiation Research Laboratory follow a standard operating procedure in the 2025 edition by Aron Habte, Manajit Sengupta, and Afshin Andreas of NREL. It governs optimal deployment within the lab, from the measurement and instrumentation data centre to the baseline system. Use cases show how that system serves solar resource work.

Instrument siting, setup, and data handling steps are spelled out so results repeat. Two parts anchor the text: the measurement data centre and the baseline system. The edition updates earlier practice for the Golden, Colorado site. Model studies of solar radiation on tracking modules are among the sources behind the approach.
doe-osti-3011902-evi-locate-user-manual:
A user manual for the EVI-LOCATE planning tool is issued by Ranjit Desai, Cabell Hodge, and Shashikiran Peddireddy of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. The tool designs electric vehicle charging sites and estimates their cost in eight steps. Users create a project, define the site, manage chargers, a transformer, and a service panel, then review the design and view the site report.

Cost assumptions rest on installer engagements, invoices from completed installations, Gordian RSMeans construction data, and General Services Administration purchase agreements. Appendices give the assumptions and calculation logic behind the estimates. The tool runs at evi-locate.nrel.gov, with a step by step video tutorial linked.
doe-osti-3012207-optimal-co-design-of-in:
Thermal and electrical networks for grid interactive efficient districts are co designed with their controls in the final report for award DE-EE0009139. Kyri Baker, Wangda Zuo, Luigi Vanfretti, and colleagues across seven institutions built an open source framework. Modelling the two networks separately misses coordinated operation gains, the team argues.

Open source microgrid models were written in Modelica, including renewable generator models REGCA, REECB, and REPCA, and validated against PSS/E results. A case study optimised a chiller plant with a local, non gradient based algorithm. Condenser water supply temperature and mass flow were tuned to cut energy use while meeting the measured cooling load.
doe-osti-3012495-advancing-tunnel-detect:
Oak Ridge report ORNL/TM-2025/4364, by Mike Kass, Charles Finney, Omar Marcillo, Monica Maceira, and Derek Splitter, dated December 2025, field-tests a new way to find buried tunnels. The team adapted vertical seismic profiling, a method that places a signal source underground, to sound waves. Their cleared test site at Oak Ridge had clay soil and a buried steel pipe standing in for a tunnel.

The pipe, 40 feet long and 3 feet wide, sat 10 feet below the surface, with shafts bored before and after it was placed. Sound pulses sent from below the pipe produced a subharmonic signal that surface geophones picked up at every sensor position. Pulses at 470 hertz and 100 decibels stayed detectable past 20 meters. Because the signal appeared only with the source below the pipe, the method can also judge tunnel depth.
doe-osti-3014214-data-summarization-and-:
Alex Pothen of Purdue University wrote this project report for award DE-SC0022260. Its topic is data summarization and inference at scale. Many science datasets no longer fit in a computer's memory. They fit even less well in a GPU's memory. The project designed algorithms that answer questions from a small, well-chosen subset of the data. They work from the subset instead of the whole flood.

Four directions structure the work. First come streaming algorithms. They keep only a solution-sized sketch as data flows past. Second come sampling methods. They keep machine learning inference accurate on small GPU memories. Third is interpretable visualization of high-dimensional clinical proteomic data for cancer detection. Fourth is hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. The quantum work splits large maximum independent set problems across D-Wave annealers and QuEra neutral-atom machines. It uses divide and conquer on graphs with good vertex separators.
doe-osti-3015666-rapid-and-efficient-dep:
A Pixelligent Technologies final report under award DE-EE0010211, submitted November 26, 2025, develops protective coatings that form while parts run. Argonne, the University of Pennsylvania, ExxonMobil, Infineum, and Winergy partnered. The Tribocoating process runs bearings and gears in a nano-enabled fluid. Friction sinters the nanocrystals into a metal-oxide film in place. No pretreatment or coating line is needed. Robert Wiacek was principal investigator.

Year one metrics were met or beaten for both lead materials. They were five-nanometer zirconia and titania. Films grew past 25 nanometers thick in two-hour rolling and sliding tests. Total wear stayed under 40 nanometers. Alumina was dropped for poor performance. Time studies show films beginning within four minutes. They are fully formed in 15 to 30 minutes of running.
doe-osti-3015701-white-paper-on-case-stu:
Four National Laboratory of the Rockies researchers, Nicholas Bartlett, Andrew Cullen, Bill Sekulic, and Kandler Smith, wrote this January 2026 white paper, numbered NLR/TP-1900-97967. Their subject is the safe setup of a second-life energy storage system. Such a system reuses electric vehicle batteries, taken out of cars, as fixed storage for a building or site.

The paper walks through the battery and its gear, covering the enclosure, heating and cooling, emergency exhaust vents, fire alarms, and gas sensors. One worked case looks at a failure in a battery pack whose modules hold up to 1,150 cells each. Readers planning to reuse old vehicle batteries get a concrete safety picture, with real failure numbers instead of general warnings.
doe-osti-3015980-csp-plant-optimization-:
Solar Dynamics LLC's final technical report for award DE-EE0009809, led by Henry W Price with Kyle Kattke and Keith Boyle among the contributors. It covers a study that ran from May 2022 to July 2025. It asks what role concentrating solar power could play in California's future grid. California law, Senate Bill 100, pushes the state toward clean electricity, yet an earlier joint agency study left this technology out.

The team assessed the technology, built cost and performance models, and ran a capacity expansion model with detailed nodes inside California. Other sections cover siting and land use. Concentrating solar power matters here because it can store heat and generate at night, filling the gap when solar panels stop. Planners get costed options for adding this kind of firm, stored solar power to the state's mix.
doe-osti-3016988-machine-tool-data-analy:
Akash Tiwari, Jaydeep Karandikar, and Vladimir Orlyanchik of Oak Ridge National Laboratory, with Chris Hamlin and Josh Davids of Scytec, wrote this CRADA final report, ORNL/TM-2026/4400, in January 2026. The project, numbered NFE-23-09833, built data analytics for machine tools. Goals were a digital twin, a live computer mirror of a machine, and predictive maintenance that warns before breakdowns.

Three data streams were combined: machine data over standard industrial protocols such as MTConnect and OPC-UA, an external vibration sensor, and the part program itself. Analytics worked at toolpath level, following the exact path of the cut. A modernized display gave operators real-time monitoring. The extra sensor data coordination with the controller computer widened what the analytics could see. Machine shops get a route to catch tool wear and faults early, instead of scrapping parts or losing spindle time.
doe-osti-3018392-demonstration-test-repo:
J A Gray and T L Orton of TD*X Associates, with C R Palmer, wrote this demonstration test report, H2C-73039 Revision 1, published October 2025. The setting is Hanford, where about fifty-four million gallons of radioactive and hazardous waste sit in underground tanks. The Waste Treatment Plant will separate that waste into a small, highly radioactive stream and a larger low-activity stream, each bound for glass.

The tests examined vacuum thermal desorption, heating waste under vacuum to drive off volatile contaminants, in support of West Area Waste Feed Test 2. Analytical tables run analyte by analyte: chlorobenzene, chloroethane, chloroform, and many more, most reported as not detected at stated limits in micrograms per kilogram. EnergySolutions staff supported the work. Feed qualification is where treatment schedules are won or lost, and this report is the measured evidence for one candidate pretreatment step.
doe-osti-3018638-trigger-system-developm:
Mattia Tinfena, supervised by Zoltan Gecse, developed trigger hardware for HGCAL cassette testing in FERMILAB-TM-2880-STUDENT. The report closes a summer 2023 internship. HGCAL is the new endcap calorimeter for CMS at the High-Luminosity LHC. Collision rates rise tenfold, and radiation levels rise with them. Silicon sensors cover the high-radiation region, arranged in cassettes of about 50 sensors each. All 525 cassettes for the hadronic section will be produced and tested at Fermilab's SiDet facility.

Tinfena's assignment was the trigger system itself. He assembled scintillator trigger planes with wavelength-shifting fibers. The fibers were connected to photomultiplier tubes by hand. The planes provide the coincidence signal that tells test electronics a particle passed through. Without that signal, cassette tests cannot separate hits from noise. The manuscript records the build in enough detail for the next intern to maintain it. Production testing of 525 cassettes rests on instruments like these.
doe-osti-3020684-lessons-learned-for-tra:
NLR report NLR/TP-6A40-97370, by Amy Rose, Christina Simeone, Ellie Estreich, and Nicholas Foss, collects lessons on one of the grid's hardest money questions. When a new transmission line benefits a whole region, who pays for it? Federal rules under FERC Orders 1000 and 1920 rest on the beneficiary-pays principle. But each regional market applies it differently, and the choices shape what gets built.

The authors build a taxonomy of transmission project types and the cost allocation methods used across United States regional markets. They then compare how the methods perform. Case material drawn from market proceedings shows where methods produced disputes, delays, or workable compromises. The report distills lessons for planners and regulators designing allocation rules for the long-range lines that reliability and new generation require.
doe-osti-3021864-dual-purpose-heating-am:
University of Maryland final technical report for DOE award DE-EE0009681, led by Vikrant Aute with James Tancabel and Al-Hussain Othman. It covers an October 2021 to September 2025 project on a thermal battery that works for both heating and cooling. The battery stores thermal energy alongside a heat pump, letting the system shift when it draws electricity and ride through peak demand periods. The report builds and validates detailed models of the combined system.

Baseline heat pump models were checked against test data from Oak Ridge National Laboratory and EPRI in both heating and cooling modes. One documented mismatch stands out. In a cold-weather heating case at 25 degrees Fahrenheit outdoors, simulated refrigerant-side capacity ran higher than measured airside capacity. That fits cabinet heat losses near 10 percent that the models do not yet include. The validation record tells future designers where the models can be trusted.
doe-osti-3022115-high-temperature-high-v:
ORNL report ORNL/TM-2026/4432, by Samuel Bell, Nathan Capps, and Mackenzie Ridley, characterizes one batch of Zircaloy-4 nuclear fuel cladding. The point is a baseline many fuel performance studies can share and trust. The batch underpins work on accident tolerant fuel coatings, loss-of-coolant accident response, and post-critical-heat-flux limits, and the team measured its behavior through controlled tensile tests at high temperature under vacuum.

The central result concerns how the material should be modeled. Although sold as stress relief annealed, the batch behaves like a transitional microstructure whose effective cold-work parameter is 0.09, far from the 0.5 value usually assumed for that heat treatment when benchmarked against the Pacific Northwest model. Chromium-coated specimens, tested for comparison, showed no distinct difference in these measurements.
doe-osti-3023139-outcomes-of-pax-sapiens:
Lauren E Charles of Pacific Northwest National Laboratory reports the outcomes of global wildlife data sharing conferences backed by PAX sapiens, in report PNNL-39091 from March 2026. The meetings served One Health security, the idea that animal, human, and environmental health data belong together. Wildlife data sit in scattered systems, and sharing them early can flag disease risks sooner.

One conference drew participants from 16 countries and tested draft standards and governance principles against European conditions. Delegates mapped what data exist where, named legal and technical hurdles to exchange, and weighed incentives for lasting participation. A stated aim was stopping a spread of incompatible databases and custom schemas that would lock the community into long-term fragmentation.
doe-osti-3025617-federal-water-managemen:
Kate Stoughton, Susan Loper, and Annie Hu of Pacific Northwest National Laboratory wrote this Federal Water Management Planning Manual, dated March 2026, for facility managers across the government. Federal sites must plan their water use, and many start with almost no end-use data. The manual walks a team from a first walk-through survey to a defensible water balance.

Most facilities meter total supply but lack submeters, so consumption by each equipment type is usually built from engineering estimates after the building walk-through. The manual points readers to a free online water balance tool from the Federal Energy Management Program that turns survey data into end-use figures. Sidebars flag resources in a directory covering baseline setting and water balance methods.
doe-osti-3028329-results-for-the-october: SWPF got October-2025-sampled, and this DOE text covers DSS salt solution. The pages detail the semiannual findings. The nuclear folks get their data. The facility was salt waste processing. The data were nuclear. The decontaminated were salt. The 2025 were October.
doe-osti-3030032-resstock-measure-docume:
Yingli Lou and Lixi Liu of the National Laboratory of the Rockies document one home retrofit option in report NLR/TP-5500-96344, dated April 2026. The note belongs to the ResStock series, which models energy upgrades across the United States housing stock. A measure here means a modeled retrofit. This one covers sealing and insulating heating and cooling ducts, the metal passages that carry air through attics, crawl spaces, and other unheated zones where leaks waste energy.

Applied across the whole stock, the upgrade saved 7 percent of total site energy, or 240 terawatt-hours in the model. Gas heating savings reached 11 percent, worth 129 terawatt-hours, and electric cooling also fell 11 percent. The method changes only duct leakage and insulation levels. It keeps duct layout and location as sampled for each home.
doe-osti-3362856-commercial-building-hva:
Samuel Harward, Saad Jajja, and Stephen Kowalski of Oak Ridge National Laboratory test rooftop heating and cooling units in CRADA report ORNL/TM-2026/4461, dated May 2026, under agreement NFE-25-10863. Carrier Corporation supplied two commercial rooftop systems for the Energy Department Commercial Building HVAC Technology Challenge. The lab job was to check, under controlled conditions, whether the units met the challenge lab test requirements for efficiency and comfort.

One key score is the sensible heat ratio, the share of total cooling that lowers air temperature rather than pulling out moisture. The test plan required an estimated ratio at or below 0.95 at the 75 degree Fahrenheit outdoor test point, corrected for the losses of on-off cycling at low building loads. Heating performance sections and steady state runs fill out the certification record.
doe-osti-3365208-mitigation-documentatio:
Desert Research Institute cultural resources report DOE/NV/89233122CNA000255-46, prepared by Megan Stueve, documents historic preservation mitigation in Area 25 of the Nevada National Security Site. Before hazardous materials could be removed from two Cold War rail vehicles, the Engine Installation Vehicle and the Manned Control Car, federal law required recording their historic fabric. Two letter reports cover the vehicles one by one.

Mitigation followed the site's agreement: updated resource assessment forms with high-quality photographs, drawings, and a letter report on significance. The vehicles served the nuclear rocket program at the E-MAD facility. The Engine Installation Vehicle survives in good shape outside, with paint wear and surface rust from open storage on Spur B. The state preservation office let the work proceed in September 2025 after its response window passed.
doe-osti-3366082-multipem-toolbox-user-m:
Los Alamos National Laboratory manual LA-UR-26-24464, by Brian J. Williams and revised September 2026, documents the MultiPEM Toolbox, a set of R scripts for explosion monitoring. Given a new event's signals across several phenomenologies, seismic, acoustic, and others, the toolbox estimates the source's unknown device parameters with uncertainty bounds. Analysts use it to characterize explosions they did not witness.

Two assessment speeds exist. Rapid assessment first calibrates forward and error models on benchmark events, then inverts the new event's data against them. Complete assessment treats the calibration parameters inside the Bayesian analysis instead of fixing them. The manual walks through code setup, forward model lists, and gradient options with worked examples. Companion journal papers carry the methodology; this volume is the operator's reference.
doe-osti-3374700-solar-energy-community-:
The final technical report for Department of Energy award DE-EE0009336 covers the SECURE project, led by the Electric Power Research Institute. Jacqueline Baum served as principal investigator. The project ran from October 2021 to September 2024. Its full name is Solar Energy CommUnity Resiliency. The goal was community microgrids that keep power flowing when the main grid fails.

The team tested candidate microgrids with detailed electromagnetic transient studies. One test checked black start, the return to service after a full outage. Others added or dropped the largest motor, generator, or load while islanded. Capacitor switching and fault clearing were also on the test list. Each case had to hold voltage and frequency inside set limits. The report runs to 172 pages of methods and results.
doe-osti-3375047-fastmath5-scidac-instit:
A final report for Department of Energy award DE-SC0021226 closes the MIT share of the FASTMath SciDAC-5 Institute. Youssef M. Marzouk led the MIT team. The project ran from September 2020 to September 2025. FASTMath builds math methods and software for very large simulations of physical systems. The MIT group worked on Bayesian inference, uncertainty checks, and smart data gathering for models that cost too much to run often.

Their main tool is MParT, a transport map toolkit. It runs in Python, Julia, and MATLAB, with GPU support through Kokkos. Transport maps let users estimate densities, fit models, and speed up Markov chain sampling. Later work added quantization methods that shrink a large data set to a small weighted point set. The error of that summary is scored by maximum mean discrepancy.
doe-osti-3377717-idaho-national-laborato:
Kyle P. Freund of the Idaho National Laboratory Cultural Resource Management Office wrote this environmental and geoarchaeological context report, INL/RPT-26-89936, in January 2026. It describes the land the laboratory occupies, the Pioneer Basin, a high-altitude cold desert of shrub steppe. Elevations run from 4,780 feet at Mud Lake to 7,550 feet at the summit of Big Southern Butte, with average yearly precipitation of about 23 centimeters.

The report builds the deep background that archaeology on the site needs. It covers present climate, then traces wetter and drier cycles through lakebed evidence around Mud Lake, where lake levels swung sharply between climate phases. In cooler, wetter periods the lake was ringed by wetland, wet meadow, and riparian communities like those near the Camas National Wildlife Refuge today.
doe-osti-3383038-rfid-enabled-tamper-ind:
Los Alamos National Laboratory technology brief LA-UR-26-26319, issued July 22, 2026 and authored by Dharmesh N. Patel, describes an RFID-enabled tamper-indicating seal at technology readiness level 4. The invention disclosure number is S196878. Such seals guard sensitive materials, valuable equipment, and critical shipments between inspections.

Standard seals must be checked by eye. A careful removal attempt may leave little visible damage. Inspectors can therefore miss tampering or disagree about it. This smart adhesive seal turns even subtle tampering into a lasting digital record. It reports its identity and status wirelessly through standard radio-frequency identification readers. That gives staff a faster, more consistent check that a protected asset has stayed sealed. The settings run from shipping yards to nuclear facilities.
doe-osti-3384943-seal-wire-verifier-syst:
Oak Ridge National Laboratory's Seal Wire Verifier System test plan, ORNL/SPR-2026/4501 from June 2026, comes from the Nuclear Nonproliferation Division. Six authors are printed: Alexander Enders, Landon Crawford, Justin Keister, Kyle Reed, Hongbin Sun, and Brett Witherspoon. The system verifies seal wires, the loops inspectors thread through closures to prove a container has not been opened.

The plan governs testing the verifier across different environmental conditions while getting the most out of a limited stock: only 15 seals are available for tests. It weighs questions such as the maximum length of wire over which the system can still detect the seal's presence. A test plan is a promise about method written before results exist, so later performance claims can be checked against it.
doe-osti-3387407-tank-14h-preliminary-ce:
Savannah River National Laboratory report SRNL-STI-2026-00181, Revision 0, dated May 2026, presents sample analyses for Tank 14H. The analyses come ahead of a preliminary cease waste removal decision. J. R. Dekarske and W. C. Benson are the authors. Savannah River Mission Completion, the organization running waste removal and tank closure at the site, asked the laboratory to characterize the tank's contents. The request supports closure.

Characterization is the gate step in tank closure. Before removal stops and a tank moves toward grouting and closure, its remaining waste must be sampled and analyzed. The closure case then rests on measured chemistry. The executive summary frames this volume as that evidence for Tank 14H. The Shielded Cells Operations group handled transfers. The laboratory's analytical and nuclear measurements groups ran the analyses.
doe-osti-3388182-instrumentation-and-sam:
Instrumentation and Samples, CRADA final report NLR/TP-5K00-99786 from July 2026, closes Project 4 under the long-running agreement CRD-12-00480. Nathan Neale is the National Laboratory of the Rockies technical contact and cited author. Funding came from the Department of Energy's Office of Science, through the Basic Energy Sciences program's division for chemical sciences, geosciences, and biosciences.

The title is deliberately plain: the project's work was the instrumentation itself and the samples measured with it, the support layer under a larger basic science collaboration. Such projects supply the measured data other teams publish on. The final report records Project 4's completion at the summary level the agreement's public closeout allows, with the laboratory's contribution stated and the project closed.
doe-osti-3388188-submitting-a-standard-c:
Submitting a Standard Compliance Annual Report is a July 2026 user guide in the EPAct State and Alternative Fuel Provider Fleet Program. It walks a covered fleet through its yearly filing in the Compliance Reporting Tool. The annual report is how fleets prove they met the program's rules for a model year. Those rules govern alternative fuel vehicle purchases.

Six steps structure the filing. A fleet chooses a model year and calculates the AFV-acquisition requirement. It reports creditable vehicle acquisitions and biodiesel fuel purchased. It reports alternative fuel investments across infrastructure, non-road equipment, and emerging technology. Then it reviews and submits, with banked credits accounted. A second half repeats the pattern for exemption requests. It runs from reporting the vehicles claimed to submitting the supporting documentation.
doe-osti-3393578-engineering-scale-valid:
Helios-NRG, LLC delivers the final report for grant DE-FE0032103 on engineering-scale validation of a novel algae carbon dioxide capture and bioproducts technology. Fred Harrington was principal investigator. The project ran from October 1, 2021 to October 31, 2025 with total funding of 2,499,030 dollars, of which 1,999,228 was federal. The funding call sat in the Office of Fossil Energy's algae engineering-scale testing area.

The partner list shows the value chain. The University of Buffalo worked on the gas-liquid contactor that dissolves carbon dioxide into the algae culture and on identifying and mitigating bio-contamination. The Bozeman Fish Technology Center analyzed and produced algae feed blends, which the Conservation Fund's Freshwater Institute then field-tested for trout growth. Craft Nutrition Consulting supported nutraceutical products, and Snapshot Energy performed the life cycle analysis.
doe-osti-3394086-integral-experiment-exe:
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory report LLNL-TR-2020894, dated July 2026, documents the execution of an integral criticality experiment: IER 519. It is the TEX-Hanford configuration with iron, at design stage CED-3b. Five authors are printed: J. Glesmann, J. Morgan, R. Sanchez, T. Grove, and Z. Lemke. TEX experiments are thermal and epithermal assemblies built from plutonium, moderated and reflected. They are used to validate nuclear data.

The middle chapters describe the hardware in detail. They cover plutonium-aluminum and aluminum surrogate plates of the ZPPR type, TEX fuel trays, and diluent layers.
